subject.title: Ensure transcript-to-client delivery consistency for channel-scoped sessions

question: What durable delivery-state contract should OpenClaw add for channel-scoped transcript entries: a transcript-entry ledger, an extension of delivery_queue_entries, or a different session-state projection?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but schema ownership, adapter reconciliation semantics, idempotent redelivery policy, and Control UI/API shape are compatibility-sensitive product decisions across core and channel boundaries.

options.title: Design Generic Ledger First
options.body: Add a SQLite-backed transcript delivery ledger tied to outbound receipts and adapter reconciliation, then expose per-entry status in session APIs and Control UI.

options.title: Accept Queue Mitigations Only For Now
options.body: Keep this issue open while landing narrow recovery mitigations such as the related ambiguous-queue PR until maintainers commit to the broader delivery-state surface.

options.title: Split Runtime And UI Work
options.body: Track a runtime-ledger/API design separately from the Control UI status surface if one issue is too broad for implementation review.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Ledger First
recommendation.body: Add a SQLite-backed transcript delivery ledger tied to outbound receipts and adapter reconciliation, then expose per-entry status in session APIs and Control UI.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest history across outbound delivery queue storage, recovery, SQLite migration, and related hardening decisions.
